fewShotPolicy.rationale: Keeps parity with TRAIN-03's already-validated zero-shot design; revisit only if TA3's capability gate fails on a category few-shot could plausibly fix.

determinismCaveat: temperature=0.0 is Gemini's minimum/most-deterministic setting, but Google's own documentation does not guarantee bit-exact determinism across identical calls the way local greedy decoding did for the closed Gemma baseline (TRAIN-03). TA3's benchmark design must tolerate and report this rather than assume single-call results are fully reproducible.
maxOutputTokensRationale: Derived from the closed Gemma-3-4B baseline's observed average output length on this exact task contract (1,009.4 characters — reports/baseline/gemma-3-4b-it-v1/error-analysis.md), approximately 250 tokens at a ~4 chars/token estimate, with a ~4x safety margin for longer cases and Gemini's own formatting overhead. This is a placeholder estimate carried over from a different model on the same task; TA3 should record Gemini's actual observed output length and revise this value if it diverges materially.
regionAvailabilityCaveat: europe-west1 is a supported Vertex AI region for Gemini generally, but specific model-tier availability is version-dependent (see ADR-002 References Reviewed). Confirm gemini-2.5-flash is available in europe-west1 before TA3's live benchmark run.
schemaCompatibilityNote: uniqueItems (present in the original TA2 draft under bullCase/bearCase.evidenceFields) was removed 2026-08-28 after TA3's first live-call smoke test: google-genai's client-side types.Schema (Vertex AI's supported OpenAPI 3.0 subset) has no uniqueItems field and rejects it with a pydantic ValidationError before any network call is made (zero cost, but zero-call otherwise). Vertex AI structured output cannot enforce array-item uniqueness; if evidenceFields duplicate-value rejection is still required, it must be enforced downstream (e.g. TRAIN-02 validator) rather than in this request schema. A second live call (still zero cost, request rejected before generation) then surfaced a second incompatibility: Vertex AI requires an explicit `type` alongside every bare `enum` node, unlike JSON Schema; the adapter now infers `type: "string"` for every string-valued enum.
thinkingBudgetNote: gemini-2.5-flash performs 'thinking' (extended internal reasoning) by default, and thoughts + visible output share the same maxOutputTokens budget. TA3's third live call (first real generation, real spend) observed thoughts_token_count=767 vs. candidates_token_count=242 against maxOutputTokens=1024 -- finish_reason=MAX_TOKENS, response truncated mid-JSON before this fix. thinkingBudget=0 disables thinking outright: this task is deterministic structured extraction over already-computed evidence (temperature=0.0's own stated goal), not a task that benefits from multi-step reasoning, so the tokens thinking would consume are pure cost/latency with no observed accuracy benefit for this contract. Revisit only if a future benchmark run shows a real accuracy gap thinking would plausibly close.
